title: Review of c11's ringed active-nematic rods (SIBMD): replicated on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (s ring rim/core 1.49 / 1.57, 89/130 and 111/150 membrane-like; 25 persistent splits each, gen 4); chis=0 leaves a diffuse fill (0.93, 0/130) with identical motion and division (Supported, ring passive)
summary: Looked at ring_seed0.png and fission_strips_seed2.png, then ran the claimed world.py on fresh seeds 3 and 4 and a chis=0 twin on seed 3 (128^2, T=1000, labkit). Surfactant s, labkit radial: rim/core 1.49 and 1.57, rim/outside 2.10 and 2.14, 89/130 and 111/150 individuals membrane-like (rerun/seed4/radial.png peaks at rho~0.85 in the rim band); chis=0: rim/core 0.93, rim/outside 1.38, 0/130 membrane-like, peak at the core. Rods swim and divide exactly as in the colony world (53 and 45 long-lived tracks >= 1 BL, max 3.4 and 4.6; 25 persistent splits each, generation 4, merges 11 and 10), and the chis=0 twin has the same motion and splits, confirming that the ring does no work (as the claim says). Note: a first attempt at the twin used the wrong parameter name and reproduced the claim world; it was discarded and re-run with chis=0.

verdicts.limitation: The ring is passive (s does not act back), so B is a structural layer, not one that does work; rim/core on seed 3 (1.49) sits at the 1.5 bar, and about 30% of individuals are not membrane-like. The M and D controls (zeta=0) are the parent's, which I re-ran for seed 3 in my colony review.
